test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 27 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Suppose Ram has placed a ball in front of a concave mirror of focal length (f) at various distances (u) and he has measured the corresponding image distances (v). From the values of u and v, Ram is able to plot a graph of 1/v against 1/u. From the graph, Ram has observed that x intercept and y intercept are 0.1 cm and 0.11 cm, respectively. Then the focal length of the mirror is:
solution:
__**Concept:**__

**Concave Mirror and Graph Analysis:**

__
 
• The relationship between object distance (u), image distance (v), and focal length (f) of a concave mirror is given by the mirror formula:
 
• **Mirror Formula:** (1)/(f) = (1)/(v) + (1)/(u) 
 
• When plotting a graph of (1)/(v) against (1)/(u) , the intercepts can provide the focal length.
 
• The x-intercept represents (1)/(f) and the y-intercept also represents (1)/(f) .
 
• **SI Unit:** The SI unit of focal length is meter (m), but in this context, we use centimeters (cm).
 
• **Dimensional Formula:** The dimensional formula for focal length is [L].

 

**Calculation:**__

Given,

x-intercept = (1)/(u) = 0.1 cm⁻¹

y-intercept = (1)/(v) = 0.11 cm⁻¹

Using the intercepts to find the focal length (f),

⇒ (1)/(f) = x{-intercept} = 0.1 

⇒ f = (1)/(0.1) = 10 cm

Similarly,

⇒ (1)/(f) = y{-intercept} = 0.11 

⇒ f = (1)/(0.11) approx 9.09 cm

Taking the average of both values,

⇒ f = (10 + 9.09)/(2) approx 9.55 cm

**∴ The focal length of the mirror is 9.55 cm.**
